mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the month following the rate hike are not statistically lower than the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive as investors anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate crosses above 2.0% in a rolling 3-month window
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-inflation crossing, 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS exceeding 2% suggests strengthening labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase of > 2% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative in 80% of PAYEMS > 2% events (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 quarterly demand exceeds INDPRO supply by more than 5% of the prior quarter's gap, the S&P 20-day forward return turns positive as market anticipates sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% of previous quarter's (GDPC1 - INDPRO)
failure_condition: Over 100 instances, the 20-day return is not statistically higher than zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of 3% or more indicates softening manufacturing capacity, which typically precedes S&P 20-day negative returns as investors price in production constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline of > 3% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive in 70% of INDPRO < 3% declines (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for 4 consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return turns negative as higher labor market participation is associated with tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly average < 4% for 4 months in a row
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative in such regimes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of FEDFUNDS below 1%, the S&P 60-day forward return is positively correlated with the 6-month change in FEDFUNDS, reflecting lower real rates and increased investment.
failure_condition: 6-month rolling correlation between FEDFUNDS change and 60-day forward return < 0.3 in magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS falls by more than 10% from its peak in the current quarter, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative as investors anticipate inventory drawdowns and soft demand.
candidate_trigger: 3-month RSAFS MA down > 10% from quarter peak
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not fall in 80% of such events (p-value > 0.05).
